A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynWorld and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ToolBench and HotpotQA evaluations, component ablations, and analyses of scenario volume and optimization iterations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for Qwen2-72B-Instruct in Table 1.

M1.justification: Scenario synthesis, MCTS exploration, and joint refinement of action descriptions and workflows are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the refinement prompts are retained; the additional evaluation backbone does not introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ToolBench multi-tool tasks and HotpotQA multi-hop question answering using Google Search. The synthetic-scenario and virtual-versus-real analyses also retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ReAct, Self-Refine, EasyTool, and DRAFT. The added Qwen2-72B-Instruct block evaluates this same comparator set; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen2-72B-Instruct as a third evaluation backbone alongside GPT-4-turbo and Qwen-long. Metrics and the existing experimental settings in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The workflow/description ablations in Table 2, scenario-volume analysis in Figure 3, and iteration/generalization analysis in Figure 4 are unchanged. No additional robustness test or supplementary analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new model results use the existing point-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds results for five methods using Qwen2-72B-Instruct. SynWorld achieves 58.52 ToolBench PASS, 73.00 WIN, and 58.70 HotpotQA F1, leading that model block. Previously reported table values and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions and Equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. Equation (4) moves between pages without mathematical revision; neither version adds proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about synthesizing multi-action scenarios, refining action knowledge through MCTS, and generalizing learned knowledge to real tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of workflow–description synergy, scalability, and diminishing returns are retained. The limitations concerning benchmark breadth, computational costs, and text-based knowledge representation are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same setup details, prompts, and pseudocode, including MCTS width 3, similarity threshold 0.6, 200 scenarios, 15 iterations, and the 6–8 million-token estimate. The code link is unchanged; no further implementation guidance accompanies the new model results.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds citations to Large Knowledge Model (Chen, 2023), Effective Tool Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Data Analysis (Zhang et al., 2024), and AweCita (Zhao et al., 2024b), with corresponding references. The surrounding research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments section and makes a small footnote-punctuation adjustment. The scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show concrete action-description and workflow examples. Table 1 expands to include the third backbone and is resized. Other figures and tables retain their content, while pagination and text placement change.

improvement.justification: The added Table 1 comparison modestly strengthens empirical support by showing SynWorld leading the same four baselines across all three metrics with a third backbone. The revised overview makes its outputs more concrete. The gain is limited because the added model receives no further setup documentation or uncertainty reporting, while the remaining scientific evidence is unchanged.
